@@@@ FILE tools/pack/extract.mjs | text | 3042 | edf91797c15221e29d361039b049e8ffee3bdd126b32585cf0d0c993147815a6
// Unpacks "project instructions.md": writes every embedded file and checks its SHA-256.
//   node extract.mjs "<project instructions.md>" [outDir=.] [--memory <dir>] [--force]
// Files packed as @memory/… go to --memory (Claude's memory folder), or to .bootstrap/memory/ without it.
// An existing file that differs is kept unless --force. Exit 1 if any checksum fails.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const take = k => { const i = args.indexOf(k); return i < 0 ? undefined : args.splice(i, 2)[1]; };
const memDir = take('--memory');
const force = args.includes('--force');
const [src, outDir = '.'] = args.filter(a => a !== '--force');
if (!src) {
  console.error('usage: node extract.mjs "<project instructions.md>" [outDir] [--memory <dir>] [--force]');
  process.exit(2);
}

const lines = fs.readFileSync(src, 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').split('\n');
const sha = b => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
const HEAD = /^@@@@ FILE (.+) \| (text|text-crlf|base64) \| (\d+) \| ([0-9a-f]{64})( \| noeol)?$/;
let i = lines.indexOf('@@@@ PAYLOAD BEGIN');
if (i < 0) throw new Error('no payload found in ' + src);
const n = { written: 0, same: 0, dirs: 0, kept: [], bad: [] };
for (i++; i < lines.length && lines[i] !== '@@@@ PAYLOAD END'; i++) {
  const line = lines[i];
  if (line.startsWith('@@@@ DIR ')) {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(outDir, line.slice(9)), { recursive: true });
    n.dirs++;
    continue;
  }
  const m = HEAD.exec(line);
  if (!m) {
    if (line.trim()) throw new Error(`line ${i + 1}: expected a FILE header, got: ${line.slice(0, 80)}`);
    continue;
  }
  const [, rel, enc, size, hash, noeol] = m;
  const body = [];
  for (i++; lines[i] !== '@@@@ END'; i++) {
    if (i >= lines.length) throw new Error('unterminated entry: ' + rel);
    body.push(lines[i]);
  }
  let buf;
  if (enc === 'base64') buf = Buffer.from(body.join(''), 'base64');
  else {
    let t = body.join('\n') + (noeol ? '' : '\n');
    if (enc === 'text-crlf') t = t.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n');
    buf = Buffer.from(t, 'utf8');
  }
  if (buf.length !== +size || sha(buf) !== hash) {
    n.bad.push(rel);
    continue;
  }
  const dst = rel.startsWith('@memory/')
    ? path.join(memDir ?? path.join(outDir, '.bootstrap', 'memory'), rel.slice(8))
    : path.join(outDir, rel);
  if (fs.existsSync(dst)) {
    if (sha(fs.readFileSync(dst)) === hash) { n.same++; continue; }
    if (!force) { n.kept.push(rel); continue; }
  }
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dst), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(dst, buf);
  n.written++;
}
console.log(`${n.written} files written, ${n.same} already identical, ${n.dirs} folders, ${n.bad.length} checksum failures`);
if (n.kept.length) console.log(`kept ${n.kept.length} existing files that differ (pass --force to overwrite):\n  ${n.kept.join('\n  ')}`);
if (n.bad.length) {
  console.error(`CHECKSUM FAILED (this file was altered after packing):\n  ${n.bad.join('\n  ')}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md | text | 4004 | 77b378463f3349852319fbd0d5719cc447bc9e2bf67d2b239da80a3b06dc4ab5
# ElevenLabs: first-connect checklist

Voice (narration + character lines) uses the ElevenLabs API, called directly with `fetch` from `tools/episode.mjs` — no MCP. Run this checklist once, the first time a copy of this project has no working `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.

Until the key is working, everything except real voice-over works: ideas, scripts, shot lists, `draft` previews, short shots with Python sound, audits, reviews and preview renders. If the user asks for a finished episode before the key works, go up to the preview (CLAUDE.md long-form step 4), then ask them for a key.

## Choices made at setup

- Narrator voice: default pick for the content language, chosen at setup — run step 3 now and confirm the pick, unless the setup answer was "audition first", in which case run step 3 as a full audition before picking anything

## Steps

1. **Get a key.** Ask the user for their ElevenLabs API key (elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys → Create API Key). Save it to `.env` at the project root as `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=...` (the `.env` file is gitignored — never commit it or print it back in full).

2. **Smoke test.** `GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices` (header `xi-api-key: <key>`) must return 200. If it 401s, the key is wrong; if it 403s with `missing_permissions`, the key is scoped — note which permissions are missing (voices/TTS access is enough to run the pipeline; `user_read` is only needed for an automatic balance check, see step 5).

3. **Pick house voices.** `tools/episode.mjs`'s `HOUSE_VOICES` needs a narrator, a male and a female voice, in the project's content language. The account's own saved voices (`/v1/voices`) may not have what's needed — search the full public library instead:
   - `GET /v1/shared-voices?language=<lang>&use_cases=narrative_story` for narrator candidates (calm/warm, not "excited" or "upbeat" — the house style is unhurried).
   - `GET /v1/shared-voices?language=<lang>&gender=male` / `&gender=female` for the secondary voices (young, casual/natural).
   - Pull 3–4 candidates per role, fetch each one's `preview_url`, and let the user pick by ear — don't choose a voice the user hasn't heard.
   - A public-library voice_id can be used directly in a TTS call without first "adding" it to the account.

4. **Measure the real cost before committing.** Credit cost per character varies by model and isn't published cleanly — measure it: call `POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/with-timestamps` with a short (~15 s) test script in the project's content language and the chosen narrator voice and model (`eleven_v4` unless the user asks otherwise), then diff `GET /v1/usage/character-stats?start_unix=<ms>&end_unix=<ms>&include_live_requests=true` before/after (its `usage.All` series updates within a few seconds). Report the measured credits/char to the user and update the `CREDITS_PER_CHAR` constant and the Voice section of `CLAUDE.md`.

5. **Balance checks.** `GET /v1/user/subscription` gives the real remaining balance, but needs the `user_read` permission. If the key doesn't have it, tell the user to check elevenlabs.io/app/subscription manually, or to create a key with that permission added, before any `/stickman` credit checkpoint.

6. **Finish.**
   - Update `HOUSE_VOICES` in `tools/episode.mjs`, the **Voice** section of `CLAUDE.md`, and `public/episodes/pipetest/episode.json` (`voice.id`) if it exists.
   - Replace the memory file `project-elevenlabs-pending.md` with a short `reference` memory: "ElevenLabs connected `<date>`, narrator `<voice>`, measured `<rate>` credits/char." Update its line in `MEMORY.md`.
   - Tell the user what was checked, which voices were picked, and the measured cost.

## Costs to keep in mind

- Voice: credits/char varies by model — don't assume 1:1. See step 4 for how to measure it for real.
- Re-running `node tools/episode.mjs sections <slug>` is free; only `node tools/episode.mjs voice <slug>` spends credits, and only for sections that don't already have a `file`.
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/FISH_SETUP.md | text | 2309 | 7e128cb13f0a80f2fcd9088152006d9401705299ade479e15c4222fc240aeedf
# Fish Audio: thumbnail-mode first-connect checklist

Fish Audio is used only for `fish`-mode thumbnail image generation (GPT Image 2.5 via Fish's media API) — see CLAUDE.md step 10. Voice does not use Fish; see `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md` for that.

Run this checklist once, the first time Fish tools are available in a session, if the thumbnail mode is `fish`. Their tool names end in `get_media_model`, `list_media_models`, `create_media_upload`, `get_credit_balance`, `list_my_workspaces`. If they appear only as deferred tools, load them with ToolSearch first.

Run this checklist again whenever the Fish account changes: the thumbnail reference keys must be reachable from the connected team.

## Choices made at setup

- Thumbnails: `fish` mode (the default) — run steps 1–2 now

## Steps

1. **Thumbnail model.**
   1. Call `get_media_model` with the `model_id` in `thumbnails/config.json` (`gpt-image-2.5-flare`).
   2. Check that it accepts the `parameters` there (16:9, 2K, medium) and `ref` image inputs, and keep its `parameter_schema`.
   3. If the model is gone or renamed, call `list_media_models`, propose the closest GPT Image model, and ask before you change `config.json`.

2. **Thumbnail references.** The `object_key`s in `thumbnails/refs/refs.json` belong to the Fish workspace the project was packed from, so upload the three images again, in order. Uploads are free.
   1. `list_my_workspaces` gives the `workspace_id`.
   2. For each `thumbnails/refs/<file>`, call `create_media_upload` with `file_name` (`ref1_paused.webp`, etc.), the exact byte size and `image/webp`.
   3. PUT the file to the returned `upload_url`: `curl.exe -X PUT -H "Content-Type: image/webp" --data-binary "@thumbnails/refs/<file>" "<upload_url>"`.
   4. Write each new `object_key` into `refs.json`, keeping the order, and set `uploaded` to today's date.

3. **Finish.**
   - Add "Last run: <date>, team <name>" under the title of this file and keep the file, for the next account change.
   - Tell the user what was checked, what changed, and what it cost.

## Costs to keep in mind

- Thumbnails (`fish` mode): 1,601 credits per 2K variant, so 3 variants are about 4.8k per episode.
- Fish AI video models are not used for episodes. A clip costs 1.4k–53k credits, and the procedural engine is free.
@@@@ END

@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/stickman.md | text | 4003 | 97ccf6c703694ba529fdc80459dc191e907299a248e78b250bafbd28ef4b3e61
---
description: Make a full "What If" stickman episode from a topic, then generate its 3 thumbnails
argument-hint: <video topic, e.g. What If You Could Swap Places With Anyone>
---

# /stickman: topic → finished video + 3 thumbnails

Topic: **$ARGUMENTS**

If the topic is empty, ask for one and stop.

Make one complete narrated episode about this topic with the saved hero, then generate its 3 thumbnails. Follow `CLAUDE.md` ("Making a narrated episode") step by step; this command only fixes the choices below. Keep a task list for the whole run.

## Fixed choices

- **Hero:** the saved character, the `hero` entry in `src/cast.ts`, exactly as it is. Don't change the outfit, and keep its signature colour off everyone else (CLAUDE.md, "… belongs to the hero").
- **Idea:** the topic replaces the idea step. Skip candidate generation and pitching. Shape it into a "What If" title (keep the user's wording when it already is one), run `python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py "<title>"`, and mention any close competitor title in the summary.
- **Slug:** short kebab-case from the title, not already used in `public/episodes/`.
- **Length:** 8–10 minutes unless the user's topic says otherwise.
- **Voice, music, look:** the house defaults in `CLAUDE.md` and memory.

## Run

1. **Script** (`docs/story/COLA_ROTEIRO.md`; open `STORY_BLUEPRINT.md` only at the § it names): beat sheet, script, plant ledger, fact check and score in `script_notes.md`.
2. **Shot list:** `episode.json`, generated from `tools/episodes/<slug>.py` (copy `_modelo.py`; helpers in `kit.py`), then `node tools/episode.mjs draft <slug>`, `npm test`, `node tools/qa.cjs audit <slug>` and `node tools/episode.mjs check <slug>` (vo text: tags, SSML, raw numbers — CLAUDE.md Voice step 5.0). Fix every error, then self-certify STORY_BLUEPRINT.md §9's "Tags de áudio e fala" group by eye — `check` is mechanical and won't catch a misplaced or mismatched tag.
3. **One checkpoint before spending credits.** Check the ElevenLabs credit balance (`GET /v1/user/subscription`; if the API key lacks `user_read`, ask the user to check elevenlabs.io/app/subscription or widen the key) and show the user, in one message:
   - the title and a short synopsis;
   - the script score and the path to `script.md`;
   - the credit estimate: voice (`node tools/episode.mjs sections <slug>` prints it, ~0.4 credits/char on eleven_v4 — see CLAUDE.md Voice) plus thumbnails (3 × the per-image cost in `thumbnails/config.json`, fish mode only).

   Wait for one OK. That OK covers the voice and the 3 thumbnails; don't ask again for either. If the balance is too low, say so and stop there.
4. **Voice, align, pre-render review:** CLAUDE.md steps 5–7, including the independent reviewer rounds. Build only on "ready for final render".
5. **Build and check:** steps 8–9. Re-render broken ranges until the sheets are clean.
6. **Thumbnails:** step 10, with the video now finished:
   - write `thumbnails/<slug>/brief.json` with exactly 3 variants (one scene per variant, drawn from the episode's strongest moments), then `node tools/thumb-prompt.mjs <slug>`;
   - `fish` mode: run `estimate_image_edit`, then submit all 3 jobs (already approved at the checkpoint), poll them together, and save each to `thumbnails/<slug>/out/<id>_2k_medium.png`. Review each at full size and at ~360 px; regenerate one only if it fails the step-10 checks (spelling, hero colour, stickman-only cast, no stray text), and only within the approved credits;
   - `chatgpt` mode: send `CHATGPT.md` and the three prompt files instead.
7. **Update `final/README.md`** with the new episode row.

## Deliver

Keep the final message short:
1. send the video, `final/<Episode title>.mp4`, with SendUserFile (`display: "render"`);
2. send the 3 thumbnails with SendUserFile in one call, captioned A / B / C with their text;
3. one or two lines: title, length, and any warning you accepted. Ask which thumbnail to pick (`node tools/thumb-prompt.mjs <slug> --pick <id>`).
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/pack/header.md | text | 24538 | 2bd9080b33f9e34964c7fadd17ddd8068a223444b1124d50b183730842cde64f
# Project instructions: 3D Stickman Long

**Claude: read only lines 1–{{HEADER_END}} of this file.** Everything after that is the packed project ({{SIZE_MB}} MB). If the user typed **start**, follow "For Claude: what start means" below.

This one file rebuilds the 3D Stickman Long production system in an empty folder. That system makes IFOLOGY-style "What If" videos with a 3D stickman hero, built in code with Remotion 4 and Three.js, with Python sound effects and ElevenLabs narration. The file holds:
- the engine, sets, cards and overlays;
- every tool;
- the style, story and research docs and the idea-engine data;
- the thumbnail template and reference images;
- Claude's project memory;
- the `/stickman <topic>` command (topic in, finished video and 3 thumbnails out).

It holds {{FILE_COUNT}} files in all, each with a checksum. It was packed on {{DATE}}. It holds no finished videos or episodes: you start with an empty channel.

## For the human

1. Make an empty folder and put this file in it. Keep the name `project instructions.md`.
2. Open a new Claude Code chat on that folder: the Code tab of the desktop app, or `claude` in a terminal there.
3. Type **start**. (If Claude asks what to start, say "follow project instructions.md".)

At {{SIZE_MB}} MB, the file is too big to paste into a chat, so it has to sit in the folder.

Claude asks four setup questions first:
- what the main character wears (with ready-made looks if you don't want to describe one);
- what language scripts, narration and overlays are written in;
- the narrator voice;
- how thumbnails are made.

Then it installs and checks everything. That takes 5–20 minutes depending on your connection (npm downloads about 1.5 GB) and on how much the outfit changes.

You need Windows 10 or 11, a GPU, and about 4 GB of free disk. Claude installs Node, Python and ffmpeg with winget if they're missing, after asking you.

**ElevenLabs** (voice) is connected afterwards:
1. Get an API key at elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys.
2. Open a new chat in the project folder and give Claude the key.
3. Claude runs `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md`: it saves the key to `.env`, picks house voices in your language, and measures the real credit cost.

**Fish Audio** is separate and optional — only needed if you picked `fish`-mode thumbnails:
1. Add the Fish Audio connector to your Claude account, or the Fish Audio MCP server to Claude Code.
2. Open a new chat in the project folder and say "Fish is connected".
3. Claude runs `docs/FISH_SETUP.md`: it checks the thumbnail model and uploads the reference images.

Everything else works before either is connected: ideas, scripts, shot lists, previews and short shots.

## For Claude: what "start" means

You are installing an existing project from this file. Every project file comes out of the payload, byte for byte, with its checksum verified. Never write a project file from memory or "improve" one while installing. The only edits you make are the ones the setup answers call for (step 7).

Never read past line {{HEADER_END}} with Read, cat or grep: the rest is {{SIZE_MB}} MB of payload. Keep a task list, and run the long installs in the background.

**Shell.** Run every command in the Bash tool (Git Bash), with forward slashes, exactly as written here: `.venv/Scripts/python`, `--props='{"view":"close"}'`. If there is no Bash tool, use PowerShell:
- write `.venv\Scripts\python`;
- pass `--props` as the path of a small JSON file (`--props=out/lab/close.json`), because PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes of inline JSON;
- write the extractor with the Write tool (step 4).

### 1. Look before you start

- The folder should contain only this file, plus `.bootstrap/` if an earlier attempt stopped. If it holds other files, tell the user and ask before going on. The extractor never overwrites a file that differs unless you pass `--force`.
- Note whether the user has already mentioned an ElevenLabs API key, and whether Fish Audio tools are already available in this session (names ending in `get_credit_balance`, `get_media_model`, …, loaded or deferred). You need both in step 9.

### 2. Ask the setup questions

Ask all four in **one** AskUserQuestion call. If the tool isn't available, ask in chat and wait.

1. Header "Outfit". Question: "What should the main character wear?"
   - **Red hoodie (Recommended)**: "The original look: red hoodie with coral trim and white drawstrings, dark purple joggers, light sneakers."
   - **Purple hoodie**: "The channel's first look: purple hoodie with lilac trim, dark joggers, light sneakers."
   - **Orange hoodie + headband**: "Bright orange hoodie with cream trim, a white sweatband, charcoal joggers, white sneakers."
   - **Yellow bomber + cap**: "Sporty: yellow bomber jacket with charcoal trim, a cream cap, charcoal pants, white sneakers."
   - The automatic "Other" option lets the user describe their own outfit.
2. Header "Language". Question: "What language should scripts, narration, overlays and thumbnails be written in?"
   - **English (Recommended)**: "The language the engine's docs and example scripts are written in."
   - **Portuguese (PT-BR)**: "Scripts, VO text, overlays and thumbnail text in Portuguese. Code, docs and comments stay in English."
   - The automatic "Other" option lets the user name any other language; the story docs (`STORY_BLUEPRINT.md`, `COLA_ROTEIRO.md`, `IDEA_ENGINE.md`, `script_analysis.md`) get translated the same way.
3. Header "Narrator". Question: "Which narrator voice should ElevenLabs use once it's connected?"
   - **Default for the chosen language (Recommended)**: "Claude picks a calm, warm narrator in that language from ElevenLabs' public voice library once connected, and confirms it with you by ear before locking it in."
   - **Audition first**: "When ElevenLabs is connected, Claude plays you free samples of 3–4 narrators in that language and you pick."
4. Header "Thumbnails". Question: "How should thumbnails be made?"
   - **Fish GPT Image (Recommended)**: "Claude generates 3 options at 2K through Fish once it's connected (about 4.8k credits per episode)."
   - **ChatGPT, by hand**: "Free: Claude writes the prompts, you paste them into ChatGPT with the 3 reference images."

There is deliberately no blue option. The lead of IFOLOGY FILMS, the channel this style is modelled on, wears a blue hoodie, and the thumbnail reference images show him in it. A blue hoodie would read as a copy of that character. If the user describes a blue hoodie under "Other", tell them this and suggest another colour; go ahead only if they insist.

### 3. Check the prerequisites

Check each of these:
- `node --version`: 20 or newer (the original used v24.16.0);
- Python 3.11 or newer (`py -3.14 --version`, `py --version` or `python --version`; the original used 3.14.3);
- `ffmpeg -version` and `ffprobe -version`;
- optional: `yt-dlp --version`, which `tools/ideas/novelty.py refresh` uses to update competitor titles.

If something is missing, ask once, then install it with winget:
- `winget install -e --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS`
- `winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.14`
- `winget install -e --id Gyan.FFmpeg`
- `winget install -e --id yt-dlp.yt-dlp`

A new install isn't on PATH until a new shell starts. Find the full path, for example under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\`, or ask the user to restart the app and type start again; this procedure picks up where it left off. If winget itself is missing, give the user the download pages and wait.

### 4. Unpack

1. Copy the extractor below into `.bootstrap/extract.mjs` exactly as written.
   - In Bash, run this from the project folder; it copies the file exactly:
     `mkdir -p .bootstrap && awk '/^```js extract\.mjs$/{f=1;next} f&&/^```$/{exit} f' "project instructions.md" > .bootstrap/extract.mjs`
   - Without Bash, write it with the Write tool.
2. Run it:

```
node .bootstrap/extract.mjs "project instructions.md" . --memory "<memory folder>"
```

`<memory folder>` is the persistent memory directory that your system prompt names, such as `C:\Users\<name>\.claude\projects\<folder>\memory`. If your system prompt names none, use `docs/memory`. After the extractor has run, add this line directly under the title of `CLAUDE.md`, above the ElevenLabs note, unless it's already there:

`Project memory (the user's preferences and decisions) lives in docs/memory/: read MEMORY.md and the files it links at the start of every session, and save new memories there.`

The extractor must print `0 checksum failures`. If any file fails, this file was changed after packing (an editor or a transfer altered it). Ask the user for a fresh copy. Never hand-write the missing files.

```js extract.mjs
{{EXTRACTOR}}
```

3. Read `CLAUDE.md`, `HOW_TO_USE.md`, `docs/STYLE.md` and the memory files now. They are the project's rules. This session started before they existed, so none of them is loaded yet. From here on, follow them as any session in this project would.

   They record the decisions of the person who built the system: dates, the `swap-pilot` episode, credit balances. Treat them as the house rules and history of this project. The swap-pilot episode itself isn't included; only its thumbnail brief ships, as the example format.

**Editing files.** Many files use CRLF line endings. Keep each file's endings as they are:
- the Edit tool does this;
- `sed -i` in Git Bash silently converts a file to LF;
- Python's `write_text` on Windows forces CRLF.

### 5. Install

1. Run `npm ci` in the background. It installs the exact versions in `package-lock.json`, about 1.5 GB.
   - npm reports some "high severity vulnerabilities" in dependencies. That is expected.
   - Don't run `npm audit fix`: it changes the pinned versions.
2. Run `npx remotion browser ensure`. It downloads the headless Chrome that Remotion renders with.
3. Create the Python environment at the project root. The build tools call `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`, so it must live there.
   - Run `py -3.14 -m venv .venv`, or use whichever Python 3.11+ you found.
   - Then run `.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install numpy==2.5.4 scipy==1.18.1`.
   - If those exact versions have no wheel for that Python, install the latest `numpy scipy` and say so in the report.
4. Run `.venv/Scripts/python -I tools/sfx/pill_sprint.py`. This writes `public/audio/pill_sprint_mix.wav`, the soundtrack of the `PillSprint` reference composition. Without it, that composition fails to load in the studio.

`episode.mjs align` needs no local model — it reads timestamps ElevenLabs already returned, so there's nothing to download here.

### 6. Run the gates

All of these must pass:
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test`: every engine self-test prints PASS.
- `node tools/qa.cjs audit pipetest`: 0 errors. `pipetest` is the small fixture episode the compositions default to. It has no audio, which is expected. One framing warning (feet out of frame) is also expected.

  if (!Buffer.from(t, 'utf8').equals(buf)) return b64();

  groups.set(g, s);
}
payload.push('@@@@ PAYLOAD END', '~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~', '');

const WHAT = {
  '(root)': '`CLAUDE.md` (the project rules), `HOW_TO_USE.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Remotion and TypeScript config',
  'src/': 'the engine (rig, Stickman, actors, cameras, materials, effects), sets, cards, overlays, the episode pipeline and its self-tests',
  'tools/': 'build, episode, QA, review, stills, thumbnail and pack tools; Python sound design, music and idea tools',
  'docs/': 'style bible, story blueprint, idea engine, reviewer brief, ElevenLabs and Fish first-connect checklists, channel research with reference frames',
  'data/': 'idea-engine data: competitor titles, beat sheets, transcripts, patterns, ideas backlog',
  'public/': `the \`${FIXTURE_EPISODE}\` fixture episode (JSON only), empty \`music/\` and \`sfx/\``,
  'thumbnails/': 'config, the prompt template, the 3 reference images, an example brief',
  'final/': 'its README (finished videos land here)',
  '.claude/': 'the `/stickman <topic>` command and the `revisor-verificacao` subagent (sonnet)',
  '@memory/': "Claude's memory for this project (extracted into the new project's memory folder)",
};
const contents = ['| Path | Files | Size | What |', '|---|---|---|---|',
  ...[...groups].map(([g, s]) => `| \`${g}\` | ${s.n}${s.bin ? ` (${s.bin} binary)` : ''} | ${(s.bytes / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB | ${WHAT[g] ?? ''} |`)].join('\n');

// The hero as packed, so the outfit step stays right after a copy changes outfits and repacks itself.
const heroBody = /\bhero: \{([\s\S]*?)\},/.exec(files.get('src/cast.ts').toString('utf8'))?.[1];
if (!heroBody) throw new Error('no hero entry in src/cast.ts');
const heroEntry = `{ ${heroBody.replace(/\/\/[^\r\n]*/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().replace(/,$/, '')} }`;
const heroField = k => new RegExp(`\\b${k}: '([^']+)'`).exec(heroBody)?.[1];
const heroGrep = [...new Set(['hoodie', heroField('top'), heroField('topColor'), heroField('accent')].filter(Boolean))].join('|');

const extractor = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'extract.mjs'), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\n+$/, '');
let header = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'header.md'), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')
  .replace('{{EXTRACTOR}}', () => extractor)
  .replace('{{CONTENTS}}', () => contents)
  .replace('{{HERO_ENTRY}}', () => heroEntry)
  .replace('{{HERO_GREP}}', () => heroGrep)
  .replace(/\{\{DATE\}\}/g, new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10))
  .replace(/\{\{FILE_COUNT\}\}/g, String(files.size));
header = header.replace(/\n*$/, '\n\n');
const headerEnd = header.split('\n').length - 1;
const body = payload.join('\n');
const mb = ((Buffer.byteLength(header) + Buffer.byteLength(body)) / 1e6).toFixed(1);
header = header.replace(/\{\{HEADER_END\}\}/g, String(headerEnd)).replace(/\{\{SIZE_MB\}\}/g, mb);
if (header.split('\n').includes('@@@@ PAYLOAD BEGIN')) throw new Error('header must not contain the payload marker line');
fs.writeFileSync(out, header + body);
console.log(`${path.relative(ROOT, out)}: ${files.size} files, ${dirs.length} empty folders, ${mb} MB, header ${headerEnd} lines`);
@@@@ END

// QA runner (no frames rendered):
//   node tools/qa.cjs selftest           engine self-tests (npm test)
//   node tools/qa.cjs audit <slug>       pre-render scene audit → out/<slug>/audit.json; exit 1 on errors
const path = require('path');
const fs = require('fs');
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(path.join(ROOT, 'package.json'));
const { bundle } = req('@remotion/bundler');
const { selectComposition, openBrowser } = req('@remotion/renderer');

(async () => {
  const [cmd, slug] = process.argv.slice(2);
  if (!['audit', 'selftest'].includes(cmd) || (cmd === 'audit' && !slug)) {
    console.error('usage: node tools/qa.cjs selftest | audit <slug>');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const serveUrl = await bundle({ entryPoint: path.join(ROOT, 'src/index.ts'), publicDir: path.join(ROOT, 'public') });
  const browser = await openBrowser('chrome', { chromiumOptions: { gl: 'angle' } });
  let code = 0;
  try {
    const comp = await selectComposition({
      serveUrl, id: cmd === 'audit' ? 'Audit' : 'SelfTest', inputProps: cmd === 'audit' ? { slug } : {},
      puppeteerInstance: browser, chromiumOptions: { gl: 'angle' }, timeoutInMilliseconds: 600000,
    });
    if (cmd === 'selftest') {
      const res = comp.props.results;
      for (const r of res) console.log(`${r.pass ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.pass ? '' : '  —  ' + r.detail}`);
      const failed = res.filter(r => !r.pass).length;
      console.log(`
${res.length - failed}/${res.length} passed`);
      code = failed ? 1 : 0;
    } else {
      const out = path.join(ROOT, 'out', slug);
      fs.mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, 'audit.json'), JSON.stringify(comp.props.report, null, 1));
      console.log(comp.props.text);
      code = comp.props.report.findings.some(f => f.sev === 'error') ? 1 : 0;
    }
  } finally {
    await browser.close({ silent: true });
  }
  process.exit(code);
})();
@@@@ END

// Review frames: event-anchored, labelled stills for the visual review and the independent reviewer.
//   node tools/review.mjs <slug>
// 1. runs the scene audit (out/<slug>/audit.json) for the event list
// 2. renders Episode in review mode (name tags, expected-position markers, shot/time banner):
//    - every event (swap, path jump, flow boundary): before / at / after, 960×540 each, stacked
//    - every shot: first frame after the cut + early / late / end frames, as a strip per shot (and overview sheets)
//    - flags near-uniform (blank) frames, e.g. a camera inside a wall
// 3. writes out/<slug>/review/manifest.json: each image with its shot, narration and what must be true
//
// Incremental rounds (after fixes):  node tools/review.mjs <slug> --only c8,r6,...
//   re-renders only those shots (ids, or plain shot indexes) plus the events that touch them, and keeps
//   every other image and manifest entry from the last full run. manifest.only lists what changed, so a
//   round-2 reviewer looks at just those. Refuses (asks for a full run) if the shot list or timing changed.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const slug = args.find(a => !a.startsWith('--') && args[args.indexOf(a) - 1] !== '--only');
const onlyArg = args.includes('--only') ? args[args.indexOf('--only') + 1] : null;
if (!slug || (args.includes('--only') && !onlyArg)) {
  console.error('usage: node tools/review.mjs <slug> [--only <shotId,shotId,...>]');
  process.exit(1);
}
const D = path.join(ROOT, 'public', 'episodes', slug);
const OUT = path.join(ROOT, 'out', slug, 'review');
const ep = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(D, 'episode.json'), 'utf8'));
const tmRaw = fs.readFileSync(path.join(D, 'timing.json'), 'utf8');
const tm = JSON.parse(tmRaw);
const fps = tm.fps || 30;
const timingHash = crypto.createHash('sha1').update(tmRaw).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
const shotIds = ep.shots.map(s => s.id);

// --only: resolve shot ids to indexes and check the previous full run is still valid
let only = null, prev = null;
if (onlyArg) {
  const manifestPath = path.join(OUT, 'manifest.json');
  if (!fs.existsSync(manifestPath)) { console.error('--only needs a previous full run (no manifest.json). Run without --only first.'); process.exit(1); }
  prev = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8'));
  if (prev.timingHash !== timingHash || JSON.stringify(prev.shotIds) !== JSON.stringify(shotIds)) {
    console.error('timing.json or the shot list changed since the last full run (shot times/indexes moved). Run without --only.');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  only = new Set();
  for (const tok of onlyArg.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)) {
    const i = /^\d+$/.test(tok) ? +tok : shotIds.indexOf(tok);
    if (i < 0 || i >= shotIds.length) { console.error(`unknown shot "${tok}"`); process.exit(1); }
    only.add(i);
  }
}

// keep earlier reviewer reports: out/<slug>/review_history/reviewer_report_<time>.md
const prevReport = path.join(OUT, 'reviewer_report.md');
if (fs.existsSync(prevReport)) {
  const hist = path.join(ROOT, 'out', slug, 'review_history');
  fs.mkdirSync(hist, { recursive: true });
  fs.copyFileSync(prevReport, path.join(hist, `reviewer_report_${fs.statSync(prevReport).mtime.toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')}.md`));
}
if (!only) fs.rmSync(OUT, { recursive: true, force: true });
fs.mkdirSync(path.join(OUT, 'raw'), { recursive: true });

// 1. audit (for events); errors are reported but don't stop the review frames
spawnSync('node', [path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'qa.cjs'), 'audit', slug], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: ROOT });
const audit = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'out', slug, 'audit.json'), 'utf8'));

const frameAt = (shot, t) => {
  const s = tm.shots[shot];
  const f0 = Math.round(s.start * fps), f1 = Math.round((s.start + s.dur) * fps) - 1;
  return Math.max(f0, Math.min(f1, f0 + Math.round(t * fps)));
};
const vo = i => (ep.shots[i].vo || '').replace(/\[[^\]]*\]/g, '').trim();

const jobs = [], items = [];
let render = true; // false while listing files of shots --only skips (paths only, no render job)
const job = (name, frame) => {
  if (render) jobs.push({ out: `../${slug}/review/raw/${name}`, id: 'Episode', props: { slug, review: true }, frame });
  return path.join(OUT, 'raw', name + '.jpg');
};
// an event touches its shot, and a flow also the shot it comes from
const touches = e => !only || only.has(e.shot) || (e.kind === 'flow' && only.has(e.shot - 1));

// 2a. events
audit.events.forEach((e, k) => {
  if (!touches(e)) return;
  const label = `${String(k).padStart(2, '0')}_${e.kind}_s${e.shot}`;
  let times, expect;
  if (e.kind === 'swap') {
    times = [e.t - 0.3, e.t + 0.1, e.t + 0.6];
    expect = `SWAP ${e.what}. Frame 1: both characters at their start spots, the swapper blinking. Frames 2–3: each character stands on the OTHER's dashed marker. Exactly one name tag per marker. No two tags on one spot, no character left behind.`;
  } else if (e.kind === 'jump') {
    times = [e.t - 0.2, e.t + 0.05, e.t + 0.5];
    expect = `JUMP: ${e.what}. The move should read as intended (a swap/teleport/momentum gag), not as a glitch. Nobody overlaps after it.`;
  } else if (e.kind === 'flow') {
    const prevDur = tm.shots[e.shot - 1].dur;
    const pa = frameAt(e.shot - 1, prevDur - 0.05), b0 = frameAt(e.shot, 0.05), b1 = frameAt(e.shot, 1.0);
    const files = [job(label + '_a', pa), job(label + '_b', b0), job(label + '_c', b1)];
    items.push({ label, kind: 'flow', shot: e.shot, id: ep.shots[e.shot].id, files, vo: vo(e.shot),
      expect: `FLOW into shot ${e.shot}: the camera must continue smoothly from frame 1 (end of shot ${e.shot - 1}) through frames 2–3. No jump of the image between frames 1 and 2; characters keep their places.` });
    return;
  } else return; // plain cuts need no event frames
  const files = times.map((t, j) => job(`${label}_${'abc'[j]}`, frameAt(e.shot, t)));
  items.push({ label, kind: e.kind, shot: e.shot, id: ep.shots[e.shot].id, files, vo: vo(e.shot), expect });
});

// 2b. per shot: the first frame after the cut, then early / late / end frames (a strip), so cut-ins,
//     setups and late payoffs are all visible
const STRIP = [0, 0.3, 0.65, 0.93];
const stripT = s => STRIP.map(k => (k === 0 ? Math.min(0.04, s.dur / 2) : s.dur * k));
const strips = tm.shots.map((s, i) => {
  render = !only || only.has(i);
  return stripT(s).map((t, j) => job(`shot_${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}_${'abcd'[j]}`, frameAt(i, t)));
});
render = true;
const mids = strips.map(st => st[2]);
const rendered = new Set(jobs.map(j => path.join(OUT, 'raw', path.basename(j.out) + '.jpg')));
const isNew = f => rendered.has(f);

fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'jobs.json'), JSON.stringify(jobs));
if (only) console.log(`--only: ${only.size} shots, ${items.length} events → ${jobs.length} frames`);
const r = spawnSync('node', [path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'stills.cjs'), path.join(OUT, 'jobs.json')], { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: ROOT });
const fails = (r.stdout || '').split('\n').filter(l => l.startsWith('FAIL'));
if (fails.length) console.log(fails.join('\n'));

// 3. compose: events stacked vertically at 960 px; overview sheets of mid frames
const ff = (args) => spawnSync('ffmpeg', ['-v', 'error', '-y', ...args], { stdio: 'inherit' });
for (const it of items) {
  const out = path.join(OUT, `${it.label}.jpg`);
  ff([...it.files.flatMap(f => ['-i', f]), '-filter_complex', `${it.files.map((_, j) => `[${j}]scale=960:-2[v${j}]`).join(';')};${it.files.map((_, j) => `[v${j}]`).join('')}vstack=inputs=${it.files.length}`, out]);
  it.image = path.relative(ROOT, out).replace(/\\/g, '/');
}
const shotImgs = strips.map((st, i) => {
  const out = path.join(OUT, `shot_${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}.jpg`);
  if (!only || only.has(i)) ff([...st.flatMap(f => ['-i', f]), '-filter_complex', `${st.map((_, j) => `[${j}]scale=480:-2[v${j}]`).join(';')};${st.map((_, j) => `[v${j}]`).join('')}hstack=inputs=${st.length}`, out]);
  return path.relative(ROOT, out).replace(/\\/g, '/');
});
const per = 12;
for (let p = 0; p * per < mids.length; p++) {
  const chunk = mids.slice(p * per, (p + 1) * per);
  if (only && !chunk.some(isNew)) continue; // overview sheet unchanged
  const out = path.join(OUT, `shots_${p + 1}.jpg`);
  const cols = 3;
  const rows = Math.ceil(chunk.length / cols);
  const pad = Array.from({ length: rows * cols - chunk.length }, () => chunk[chunk.length - 1]);
  const all = [...chunk, ...pad];
  ff([...all.flatMap(f => ['-i', f]), '-filter_complex',
    `${all.map((_, j) => `[${j}]scale=640:-2[v${j}]`).join(';')};${all.map((_, j) => `[v${j}]`).join('')}xstack=inputs=${all.length}:layout=${all.map((_, j) => `${(j % cols) * 640}_${Math.floor(j / cols) * 360}`).join('|')}`, out]);
}
// 2c. blank-frame check: a near-uniform picture (camera inside a wall or a prop, a missing set)
//     shows up as a tiny pixel spread after shrinking the frame to 32×18 greyscale
// --only: keep the old blank flags of images not re-rendered, re-check the new ones
const blank = only ? (prev.blank || []).filter(b => !rendered.has(path.join(ROOT, b.image))) : [];
for (const f of [...strips.flat(), ...items.flatMap(it => it.files)]) {
  if (only && !isNew(f)) continue;
  const r = spawnSync('ffmpeg', ['-v', 'error', '-i', f, '-vf', 'scale=32:18,format=gray', '-f', 'rawvideo', '-'], { maxBuffer: 1 << 20 });
  const px = r.stdout && r.stdout.length ? [...r.stdout] : null;
  if (!px) continue;
  const mean = px.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / px.length;
  const sd = Math.sqrt(px.reduce((a, b) => a + (b - mean) ** 2, 0) / px.length);
  if (sd < 8) blank.push({ image: path.relative(ROOT, f).replace(/\\/g, '/'), sd: +sd.toFixed(1) });
}
if (blank.length) console.log(`BLANK FRAMES (near-uniform picture — camera inside geometry?):\n${blank.map(b => `  ${b.image} (spread ${b.sd})`).join('\n')}`);

// --only: events of untouched shots come from the last run; the re-rendered ones replace theirs
const keptEvents = only ? prev.events.filter(e => !touches(e)) : [];
const events = [...keptEvents, ...items.map(({ files, ...rest }) => rest)]
  .sort((a, b) => a.shot - b.shot || a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
const manifest = {
  slug, generated: new Date().toISOString(),
  timingHash, shotIds,
  ...(only ? {
    only: [...only].sort((a, b) => a - b).map(i => ({ shot: i, id: shotIds[i] })),
    onlyNote: 'Incremental run: only the shots in "only" (and their events) were re-rendered. Everything else is unchanged from the last full run.',
    fullRun: prev.fullRun || prev.generated,
  } : { fullRun: new Date().toISOString() }),
  audit: { errors: audit.findings.filter(f => f.sev === 'error'), warnings: audit.findings.filter(f => f.sev === 'warn') },
  blank,
  events,
  shots: ep.shots.map((s, i) => ({
    shot: i, id: s.id, kind: s.kind === 'card' ? `card:${s.card}` : s.set, vo: vo(i), words: tm.shots[i].words,
    strip: shotImgs[i], times: stripT(tm.shots[i]).map(t => +t.toFixed(2)),
    full: strips[i].map(f => path.relative(ROOT, f).replace(/\\/g, '/')),
  })),
  overview: fs.readdirSync(OUT).filter(f => f.startsWith('shots_')).map(f => `out/${slug}/review/${f}`),
};
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, 'manifest.json'), JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 1));
console.log(only
  ? `review frames (--only): ${only.size} shots, ${items.length} events re-rendered → out/${slug}/review/ (manifest.json, "only" lists them)`
  : `review frames: ${items.length} events, ${mids.length} shots → out/${slug}/review/ (manifest.json)`);
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/sfx/episode_audio.py | text-crlf | 10320 | 1344c42a9bf0bb90b4e41b645cd04d7e7d6d156f3785c2eb0332b44dc12adf4d
"""Full episode soundtrack: narration + music (ducked under the voice) + per-set ambience +
automatic and scripted sound effects → public/episodes/<slug>/mix.wav (stems in out/audio/<slug>/).

    .venv/Scripts/python -I tools/sfx/episode_audio.py <slug>

Scripted cues: shot "sfx": [{"t": 0.4, "name": "boom", "vol": -6, "dur": 1.2}], t = seconds into the shot.
Automatic: whoosh into cards, whip/flash cuts, ticks + chime on stat overlays, hits on titles.
Music: episode "music": [{"shot": 0, "mood": "curious"}, {"shot": 14, "mood": "tension"}] or a file:
       {"shot": 0, "file": "music/my_track.mp3", "vol": -18} (path under public/).
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
from scipy.io import wavfile  # noqa: E402

import music as M  # noqa: E402
import sfxlib as S  # noqa: E402

SR = S.SR
ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..'))
slug = sys.argv[1]
D = os.path.join(ROOT, 'public', 'episodes', slug)
ep = json.load(open(os.path.join(D, 'episode.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
tm = json.load(open(os.path.join(D, 'timing.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
TOTAL = tm['total'] + 1.0
N = int(TOTAL * SR)
S.seed(42)

OUTDOOR = {'suburb', 'city', 'park', 'stadium', 'rooftop', 'apartments'}
NIGHT = {'night', 'interiorNight', 'dusk', 'rooftopNight', 'cityNight', 'stadiumNight'}


def load_wav(path):
    sr, x = wavfile.read(path)
    integer = x.dtype.kind == 'i'
    x = x.astype(np.float64)
    if integer:
        x /= 32768.0
    if x.ndim == 1:
        x = np.stack([x, x], axis=1)
    if sr != SR:
        raise SystemExit(f'{path}: expected {SR} Hz, got {sr}')
    return x


def decode(path):
    """Any audio file → float stereo at SR via ffmpeg."""
    raw = subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-i', path, '-f', 'f32le', '-ac', '2', '-ar', str(SR), '-'], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return np.frombuffer(raw, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1, 2).astype(np.float64)


class Bus:
    def __init__(self):
        self.x = np.zeros((N, 2))

    def add(self, t, y, db=0.0):
        if y.ndim == 1:
            y = S.stereo(y)
        i = int(round(t * SR))
        if i < 0:
            y, i = y[-i:], 0
        m = min(len(y), N - i)
        if m > 0:
            self.x[i:i + m] += y[:m] * 10 ** (db / 20)


vo, mus, amb, fx = Bus(), Bus(), Bus(), Bus()


def cue(spec, words, fallback=0.0):
    """Same word-cue syntax as src/episode/cue.ts: number, '@word', '@word#2', '@word+0.1'."""
    import re
    if spec is None:
        return fallback
    if isinstance(spec, (int, float)):
        return float(spec)
    m = re.match(r"^@((?:[^\W_]|')+)(?:#(\d+))?([+-][\d.]+)?$", str(spec).strip(), re.I)
    if not m:
        return fallback
    hits = [t for w, t in (words or []) if w == m.group(1).lower()]
    if not hits:
        return fallback
    n = int(m.group(2) or 1)
    return hits[min(n, len(hits)) - 1] + float(m.group(3) or 0)


# --- narration ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
draft = tm.get('draft', False)
if not draft:
    for sec in tm['sections']:
        vo.add(sec['start'], load_wav(os.path.join(ROOT, 'public', sec['file'])), 0)

# --- ambience per 3D shot (crossfaded) ------------------------------------------------------
for i, shot in enumerate(ep['shots']):
    st, du = tm['shots'][i]['start'], tm['shots'][i]['dur']
    if shot.get('kind') == 'card':
        continue
    seg = du + 0.3
    set_ = shot.get('set', 'suburb')
    night = shot.get('time') in NIGHT
    if set_ in OUTDOOR:
        a = S.ambience(seg, 0.12)
        if night:
            a = S.stereo(S.lp(S.pink(seg), 900) * 0.04, width=1)
            for c in range(int(seg * 3)):
                ch = S.osc(4300, 0.05) * np.sin(np.pi * S.t_axis(0.05) / 0.05) * 0.03
                j = int((c / 3 + 0.1) * SR)
                a[j:j + len(ch)] += S.stereo(ch, 0.5 - (c % 2))[: max(0, min(len(ch), len(a) - j))]
        if set_ == 'stadium':
            crowd = S.bp(S.pink(seg), 300, 2500) * (0.7 + 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.3 * S.t_axis(seg)))
            a += S.stereo(S.norm(crowd) * 0.15, width=1)
        if set_ == 'apartments':
            # a building fire instead of birds: roar + flame rush + wood crackle, a siren far off
            a = S.stereo(S.lp(S.brown(seg), 300) * 0.03, width=1) + S.fire_bed(seg, 0.16) + S.siren(seg, 0.05, 0.75)
    else:
        a = S.stereo(S.lp(S.pink(seg), 500) * 0.05 + S.lp(S.brown(seg), 120) * 0.04, width=1)
    amb.add(st - 0.15, S.fade(a, 0.15, 0.15), -2)

# --- sound effects ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
LIB = {
    'whoosh': lambda d: S.whoosh(d or 0.5, 2600, 500, 0.8),
    'whooshUp': lambda d: S.whoosh(d or 0.5, 500, 4000, 0.8),
    'swoosh': lambda d: S.whoosh(d or 0.25, 5000, 1500, 0.6),
    'boom': lambda d: S.boom(1.0, 0.0),
    'farBoom': lambda d: S.double_boom(0.8, 0.6),
    'thud': lambda d: S.footstep(1.0),
    'footsteps': lambda d: np.concatenate([np.vstack([S.footstep(0.7, 0.2 * (-1) ** k), np.zeros((int(0.27 * SR) - len(S.footstep()), 2))]) for k in range(int((d or 1.2) / 0.27))]),
    'gulp': lambda d: S.gulp(0.9),
    'click': lambda d: S.click(3200, 0.03, 0.6),
    'pop': lambda d: S.mouth_pop(0.7),
    'cloth': lambda d: S.cloth(d or 0.3, 0.4),
    'heartbeat': lambda d: S.heartbeat(1.0),
    'subdrop': lambda d: S.sub_drop(d or 0.9),
    'riser': lambda d: S.riser(d or 2.0),
    'swell': lambda d: S.reverse_swell(d or 0.5),
    'zap': lambda d: S.zap(3000, 0.06, 0.6),
    'crackle': lambda d: S.crackle_bed(d or 1.0, 25, 0.5),
    'wind': lambda d: S.wind_roar(d or 2.0, 0.7),
    'debris': lambda d: S.debris(d or 0.8, 0.5),
    'rustle': lambda d: S.rustle(d or 0.9, 0.4),
    'chime': lambda d: S.chime(0.45),
    'glint': lambda d: S.glint(0.4),
    'ticks': lambda d: S.ticks(d or 0.4, 26, 12, 0.18),
    'ring': lambda d: S.ringtone(d or 1.6),
    'bell': lambda d: S.school_bell(d or 2.5),
    'whistle': lambda d: S.whistle(d or 0.7),
    'groan': lambda d: S.groan(d or 1.4),
    'groanLow': lambda d: S.groan(d or 1.8, 0.3, 82.0),
}
DEFAULT_DB = {'whoosh': -9, 'swoosh': -12, 'whooshUp': -9, 'boom': -4, 'farBoom': -8, 'gulp': -2, 'chime': -8, 'ticks': -12, 'glint': -10,
              'wind': -8, 'riser': -10, 'crackle': -12, 'heartbeat': -4, 'subdrop': -8, 'click': -10, 'pop': -6, 'cloth': -10, 'footsteps': -10}

for i, shot in enumerate(ep['shots']):
    st = tm['shots'][i]['start']
    if shot.get('kind') == 'card':
        fx.add(st - 0.05, S.whoosh(0.3, 4200, 900, 0.5), -15)
    words = tm['shots'][i].get('words')
    swap = (shot.get('fx') or {}).get('swap')
    if swap:
        ts = st + cue(swap['t'], words, 0.5)
        fx.add(ts - 0.3, S.whoosh(0.3, 600, 5200, 0.6), -11)   # blink-blink charge
        fx.add(ts, S.mouth_pop(0.8), -6)                      # the swap 'pop'
        fx.add(ts, S.glint(0.4), -13)
    cut = shot.get('cut')
    if cut == 'whip':
        fx.add(st - 0.12, S.whoosh(0.3, 3000, 600, 0.9), -8)
    elif cut == 'flash':
        fx.add(st, S.glint(0.4), -12)
        fx.add(st, S.boom(0.6, 0.4), -12)
    for o in shot.get('overlays', []):
        at = st + cue(o.get('at', 0), words, 0)
        if o['type'] == 'stat':
            fx.add(at, S.ticks(0.33, 30, 12, 0.18), -14)
            fx.add(at + 0.33, S.chime(0.45), -10)
        elif o['type'] == 'title':
            fx.add(at - 0.3, S.reverse_swell(0.3, 0.5), -10)
            fx.add(at, S.boom(0.8, 0.3), -9)
        elif o['type'] == 'label':
            fx.add(at, S.click(2600, 0.03, 0.4), -14)
    for c in shot.get('sfx', []):
        name = c['name']
        if name not in LIB:
            print(f'  ! unknown sfx "{name}" in shot {i} (known: {", ".join(LIB)})')
            continue
        fx.add(st + cue(c.get('t', 0), words, 0), LIB[name](c.get('dur')), c.get('vol', DEFAULT_DB.get(name, -8)))

# --- music --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cues = sorted(ep.get('music', [{'shot': 0, 'mood': 'curious'}]), key=lambda c: c['shot'])
for k, c in enumerate(cues):
    t0 = tm['shots'][c['shot']]['start']
    t1 = tm['shots'][cues[k + 1]['shot']]['start'] if k + 1 < len(cues) else TOTAL
    seg = t1 - t0 + 1.0
    if c.get('file'):
        y = decode(os.path.join(ROOT, 'public', c['file']))
        reps = int(np.ceil(seg * SR / len(y))) + 1
        y = np.tile(y, (reps, 1))[: int(seg * SR)]
    else:
        y = M.bed(c.get('mood', 'curious'), seg)
    y = S.fade(y, 0.6 if k == 0 else 1.0, 1.0 if k + 1 < len(cues) else 2.0)
    mus.add(t0 - (0 if k == 0 else 0.5), y, c.get('vol', -17))

# duck music + ambience under the voice (smoothed envelope sidechain)
env = np.abs(vo.x).mean(axis=1)
hop = 480
e = np.array([env[j:j + hop].max() for j in range(0, N, hop)])
g = np.zeros_like(e)
for j in range(len(e)):
    target = 1.0 if e[j] > 0.02 else 0.0
    coef = 0.5 if target > (g[j - 1] if j else 0) else 0.06  # fast attack, slow release
    g[j] = (g[j - 1] if j else 0) + coef * (target - (g[j - 1] if j else 0))
duck = np.repeat(g, hop)[:N]
mus.x *= (1 - 0.55 * duck)[:, None]
amb.x *= (1 - 0.35 * duck)[:, None]

# --- master -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mix = vo.x + mus.x + amb.x + fx.x
mix -= mix.mean(axis=0)
mix = S.hp(mix.T, 25, 2).T
peak = np.max(np.abs(mix)) + 1e-9
mix = mix / peak
mix = np.tanh(mix * 1.2) / np.tanh(1.2)
mix = S.norm(mix, 10 ** (-1.0 / 20))
mix = S.fade(mix, 0.01, 0.8)

out_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, 'out', 'audio', slug)
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
for name, b in (('vo', vo), ('music', mus), ('ambience', amb), ('sfx', fx)):
    S.write_wav(os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.wav'), S.norm(b.x, 0.9) if np.any(b.x) else b.x)
S.write_wav(os.path.join(D, 'mix.wav'), mix.astype(np.float32))
rms = 20 * np.log10(np.sqrt(np.mean(mix ** 2)) + 1e-9)
print(f'mix.wav: {TOTAL:.1f} s, rms {rms:.1f} dBFS' + (' (draft timing: no narration yet)' if draft else ''))
@@@@ END

"""Procedural underscore beds (numpy only). Each mood renders one seamless 8-bar loop with
vectorised additive instruments, then `bed(mood, seconds)` tiles it to any length.
Moods: curious (playful pluck, IFOLOGY-style default), wonder, tension, action, sad.
These sit ~17 dB under the narration and duck further while the voice speaks.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

import sfxlib as S

SR = S.SR


def mtof(m):
    return 440.0 * 2 ** ((np.asarray(m, dtype=float) - 69) / 12)


def note_pluck(f: float, dur: float, bright: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Plucked string / marimba-ish tone: harmonics with faster decay up the series."""
    t = S.t_axis(dur)
    x = np.zeros_like(t)
    for h in range(1, 7):
        x += (0.6 ** (h - 1)) * bright ** (h - 1) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * h * t) * np.exp(-t * (3.5 + 2.2 * h))
    x *= np.clip(t / 0.003, 0, 1)
    return x


def note_bell(f: float, dur: float) -> np.ndarray:
    t = S.t_axis(dur)
    x = sum(a * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * r * t) * np.exp(-t * d) for r, a, d in ((1, 1, 1.6), (2.76, 0.4, 2.8), (5.4, 0.2, 4.5), (8.9, 0.08, 7)))
    return x * np.clip(t / 0.002, 0, 1)


def note_piano(f: float, dur: float) -> np.ndarray:
    t = S.t_axis(dur)
    x = sum((0.55 ** (h - 1)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * h * t * (1 + 0.0004 * h * h)) * np.exp(-t * (1.2 + 0.9 * h)) for h in range(1, 8))
    return x * np.clip(t / 0.004, 0, 1)


def pad(freqs, dur: float, cutoff: float = 1100, attack: float = 0.6) -> np.ndarray:
    t = S.t_axis(dur)
    x = np.zeros_like(t)
    for f in freqs:
        for det in (-0.004, 0.0, 0.0045):
            x += S.osc(f * (1 + det), dur, 'saw')
    x = S.lp(x / (3 * len(freqs)), cutoff, 2)
    env = np.clip(t / attack, 0, 1) * np.clip((dur - t) / 0.4, 0, 1)
    return x * env


def bass_note(f: float, dur: float, kind: str = 'sine') -> np.ndarray:
    t = S.t_axis(dur)
    if kind == 'saw':
        x = S.lp(S.osc(f, dur, 'saw'), 650, 2)
    else:
        x = np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) + 0.35 * np.sin(4 * np.pi * f * t)
    return x * np.clip(t / 0.005, 0, 1) * np.clip((dur - t) / 0.05, 0, 1) * np.exp(-t * 1.5)


def kick(level=1.0):
    d = 0.35
    t = S.t_axis(d)
    return (np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(S.glide(120, 45, d)) / SR) * np.exp(-t / 0.09)) * level


def snare(level=1.0):
    d = 0.25
    t = S.t_axis(d)
    return (S.bp(S.white(d), 1200, 7000) * np.exp(-t / 0.05) * 0.8 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * 190 * t) * np.exp(-t / 0.04) * 0.5) * level


def hat(level=1.0, open_=False):
    d = 0.18 if open_ else 0.05
    t = S.t_axis(d)
    return S.hp(S.white(d), 7000) * np.exp(-t / (0.06 if open_ else 0.015)) * level


def shaker(level=1.0):
    d = 0.08
    t = S.t_axis(d)
    return S.bp(S.white(d), 4000, 12000) * np.sin(np.pi * t / d) ** 2 * level


class Track:
    def __init__(self, bars: int, bpm: float, beats_per_bar: int = 4):
        self.beat = 60.0 / bpm
        self.len = bars * beats_per_bar * self.beat
        self.buf = np.zeros((int(self.len * SR) + SR, 2))

    def add(self, beat_pos: float, x: np.ndarray, gain: float = 1.0, pan: float = 0.0):
        st = S.stereo(x * gain, pan)
        i = int(beat_pos * self.beat * SR)
        m = min(len(st), len(self.buf) - i)
        self.buf[i: i + m] += st[:m]

    def loop(self) -> np.ndarray:
        n = int(self.len * SR)
        out = self.buf[:n].copy()
        tail = self.buf[n:]
        out[: len(tail)] += tail  # wrap ringing tails to the start: seamless loop
        return out


def chords_for(mood):
    # (root midi, chord intervals) per bar for 8 bars
    if mood == 'curious':
        prog = [(53, (0, 4, 7)), (50, (0, 3, 7)), (46, (0, 4, 7)), (48, (0, 4, 7))]  # F Dm Bb C
    elif mood == 'wonder':
        prog = [(50, (0, 4, 7, 11)), (52, (0, 4, 7)), (47, (0, 3, 7)), (43, (0, 4, 7, 11))]  # Dmaj7 E Bm Gmaj7
    elif mood == 'tension':
        prog = [(45, (0, 3, 7)), (41, (0, 4, 7)), (50, (0, 3, 7)), (40, (0, 4, 7))]  # Am F Dm E
    elif mood == 'action':
        prog = [(50, (0, 3, 7)), (46, (0, 4, 7)), (48, (0, 4, 7)), (45, (0, 4, 7))]  # Dm Bb C A
    else:  # sad
        prog = [(48, (0, 3, 7)), (44, (0, 4, 7)), (51, (0, 4, 7)), (46, (0, 4, 7))]  # Cm Ab Eb Bb
    return prog * 2


def render_loop(mood: str) -> np.ndarray:
    S.seed(1000 + len(mood))
    bpm = {'curious': 104, 'wonder': 76, 'tension': 92, 'action': 128, 'sad': 68}[mood]
    tr = Track(8, bpm)
    prog = chords_for(mood)
    b = tr.beat
    for bar, (root, iv) in enumerate(prog):
        p0 = bar * 4
        notes = [root + i for i in iv]
        if mood == 'curious':
            tr.add(p0, pad(mtof([n + 12 for n in notes]), 4 * b, 900), 0.18)
            arp = [notes[0] + 12, notes[1] + 12, notes[2] + 12, notes[0] + 24, notes[2] + 12, notes[1] + 12, notes[0] + 12, notes[1] + 24]
            for k, m in enumerate(arp):
                tr.add(p0 + k * 0.5, note_pluck(float(mtof(m)), 0.6, 0.8), 0.32, pan=-0.25 + 0.5 * (k % 2))
            for q in range(4):
                tr.add(p0 + q, bass_note(float(mtof(root - 12)), b * 0.9), 0.5)
                tr.add(p0 + q + 0.5, shaker(), 0.12, 0.3)
                tr.add(p0 + q + 0.75, shaker(), 0.07, 0.3)
            tr.add(p0, kick(0.5), 1.0)
            tr.add(p0 + 2, kick(0.4), 1.0)
        elif mood == 'wonder':
            tr.add(p0, pad(mtof(notes + [notes[0] + 12]), 4 * b + 0.3, 1400, 1.2), 0.3)
            for k in range(4):
                m = notes[(k * 2) % len(notes)] + 24
                tr.add(p0 + k + (0.5 if k % 2 else 0), note_bell(float(mtof(m)), 2.0), 0.18, pan=-0.4 + 0.27 * k)
            tr.add(p0, bass_note(float(mtof(root - 12)), 4 * b), 0.3)
        elif mood == 'tension':
            tr.add(p0, pad(mtof([notes[0] + 12, notes[0] + 13, notes[2] + 12]), 4 * b, 700, 1.0), 0.16)
            for e in range(8):
                tr.add(p0 + e * 0.5, bass_note(float(mtof(root - 12)), b * 0.45, 'saw'), 0.45)
                tr.add(p0 + e * 0.5, hat(0.6), 0.1, 0.4)
            tr.add(p0, kick(0.7), 1.0)
            tr.add(p0 + 0.75, kick(0.4), 1.0)
        elif mood == 'action':
            tr.add(p0, pad(mtof([n + 12 for n in notes]), 4 * b, 1600, 0.05), 0.2)
            for e in range(8):
                tr.add(p0 + e * 0.5, bass_note(float(mtof(root - 12)), b * 0.48, 'saw'), 0.55)
                tr.add(p0 + e * 0.5 + 0.25, hat(0.8), 0.14, 0.3)
            for q in range(4):
                tr.add(p0 + q, kick(1.0), 0.9)
            tr.add(p0 + 1, snare(), 0.45)
            tr.add(p0 + 3, snare(), 0.45)
            if bar % 2 == 0:
                for n in notes:
                    tr.add(p0, note_pluck(float(mtof(n + 12)), 0.4, 1.2), 0.18)
        else:  # sad
            tr.add(p0, pad(mtof([n + 12 for n in notes]), 4 * b, 800, 1.5), 0.15)
            for k, m in enumerate([notes[0], notes[1] + 12, notes[2] + 12, notes[1] + 12]):
                tr.add(p0 + k, note_piano(float(mtof(m + 12)), 2.5), 0.3)
            tr.add(p0, note_piano(float(mtof(root - 12)), 4 * b), 0.35)
    x = tr.loop()
    x = S.reverb(x, decay=1.4, mix=0.18, damp=5000)
    return S.norm(x, 0.8)


_cache: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}


def bed(mood: str, seconds: float) -> np.ndarray:
    if mood == 'none':
        return np.zeros((int(seconds * SR), 2))
    if mood not in _cache:
        _cache[mood] = render_loop(mood)
    loop = _cache[mood]
    reps = int(np.ceil(seconds * SR / len(loop))) + 1
    return np.tile(loop, (reps, 1))[: int(seconds * SR)]

"""Sound design for the 4 s pill-sprint shot. Event times come from src/demo/pillSprint.json,
the same file the animation reads, so picture and sound can't drift apart.

    .venv/Scripts/python tools/sfx/pill_sprint.py
writes public/audio/pill_sprint_mix.wav (+ stems in out/audio/pill_sprint/).
"""
import json
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import sfxlib as S  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..'))
TL = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src', 'demo', 'pillSprint.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
E, SH, DUR = TL['events'], TL['shots'], TL['duration']
S.seed(11)

stems = {k: S.Mix(DUR) for k in ('amb', 'foley', 'power', 'impact', 'speed', 'ui')}

# --- ambience: calm street until the launch; dips during the close-up ------------------------
amb = S.ambience(SH['D'][0] + 0.2, level=0.13)
stems['amb'].add(0.0, amb, -2)
stems['amb'].duck(SH['B'][0], SH['B'][1], -6)
stems['amb'].duck(E['launch'], DUR, -40, ramp=0.03)

# --- foley: pill handling, mouth, gulp ------------------------------------------------------
f = stems['foley']
f.add(0.06, S.click(3400, 0.03, 0.35), -6)               # pill tapped between the fingers
f.add(E['pillLift'] - 0.02, S.cloth(0.3, 0.3), -8)        # sleeve rustle as the hand rises
f.add(E['pillIn'] - 0.015, S.mouth_pop(0.6), -3)          # pill in
f.add(E['gulp'] - 0.04, S.gulp(0.9), 0)                   # GULP
f.add(E['crouch'], S.cloth(0.25, 0.35), -6)               # drops into the crouch

# --- power-up: reverse swell into the surge, heartbeat, sub drop, rising energy --------------
p = stems['power']
p.add(E['surge'] - 0.45, S.reverse_swell(0.45, 0.55), -6)
p.add(E['surge'], S.heartbeat(1.0), -4)
p.add(E['surge'], S.sub_drop(0.9, 95, 30, 0.9), -8)
p.add(E['beat2'], S.heartbeat(0.9), -6)
rise_dur = E['launch'] - E['surge']
p.add(E['surge'] + 0.05, S.riser(rise_dur - 0.05, 260, 7000, 0.5, 110), -9)


def crack_density(t):
    T = E['surge'] + t
    if T > E['launch']:
        return 0
    return 18 + 30 * (T - E['surge']) / (E['launch'] - E['surge'])


p.add(E['surge'], S.crackle_bed(E['launch'] - E['surge'] + 0.05, crack_density, 0.5), -9)
p.add(SH['B'][0] - 0.03, S.whoosh(0.22, 3000, 700, 0.45), -10)      # cut into the close-up
p.add(E['smirk'] + 0.02, S.glint(0.4), -9)                           # confident smirk sparkle

# --- impact: launch boom, debris, leaves, distant sonic boom --------------------------------
i = stems['impact']
i.add(E['launch'] - 0.012, S.boom(1.0, 0.0), 2)
i.add(E['launch'], S.whoosh(0.55, 2600, 260, 0.9, 0.0, 0.6, q=1.3), -3)
i.add(E['launch'] + 0.02, S.debris(0.9, 0.5), -4)
i.add(E['launch'] + 0.05, S.rustle(0.95, 0.35), -6)
i.add(E['launch'] + 0.12, S.double_boom(0.7, 0.6), -7)             # far down the street

# --- speed: wind roar, footfalls, passing whooshes, exit ------------------------------------
sp = stems['speed']
d0 = SH['D'][0]
sp.add(d0 - 0.03, S.whoosh(0.18, 5000, 1200, 0.7), -6)             # smash cut in
wind = S.wind_roar(DUR - d0 + 0.05, 0.75)
sp.add(d0, wind, -5)
# footfalls on the dash cycle: 3.9 cycles/s = 7.8 contacts/s, alternating sides
k = 0
t = d0 + 0.02
while t < E['exit'] + 0.1:
    sp.add(t, S.footstep(0.6, -0.15 if k % 2 else 0.15), -9)
    k += 1
    t += 1 / 7.8
# world rushing past: short whooshes sweeping right → left
for j, tw in enumerate(np.arange(d0 + 0.1, DUR - 0.1, 0.23)):
    sp.add(float(tw), S.whoosh(0.2, 1800 + 300 * (j % 3), 500, 0.35, 0.7, -0.7), -12)
sp.add(d0, S.crackle_bed(DUR - d0, 10, 0.35), -14)
sp.add(E['exit'] - 0.05, S.whoosh(0.4, 900, 4500, 0.9, -0.2, 0.9, q=1.4), -2)   # he pulls away
sp.add(E['exit'] + 0.16, S.boom(0.7, 0.35), -5)

# --- ui: ×100 callout --------------------------------------------------------------------------
u = stems['ui']
u.add(E['hud'] - 0.04, S.whoosh(0.16, 6000, 2000, 0.4), -10)
u.add(E['hud'], S.ticks(0.33, 30, 12, 0.18), -12)
u.add(E['hud'] + 0.33, S.chime(0.45), -6)

# --- mix ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
gains = {'amb': 0, 'foley': 0, 'power': 0, 'impact': 0, 'speed': -1, 'ui': -1}
master = S.Mix(DUR)
out_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, 'out', 'audio', 'pill_sprint')
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
for name, st in stems.items():
    master.buf += st.buf * (10 ** (gains[name] / 20))
    S.write_wav(os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.wav'), S.norm(st.buf, 0.9) if np.any(st.buf) else st.buf)
mix = master.master(-1.0, 1.25)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, 'public', 'audio'), exist_ok=True)
S.write_wav(os.path.join(ROOT, 'public', 'audio', 'pill_sprint_mix.wav'), mix)
